summary: 研究者比较三叠纪末前后的湖岸足迹，发现恐龙在竞争者消失后迅速占据优势、体型增大。蕨类孢子骤增支持当时发生过生态剧变，是否由撞击引发仍需寻找证据。
logic: 提出恐龙迅速崛起的问题
用湖泥足迹跨地点对照
以孢子和足迹重建剧变

paragraphs.brief: 撞击假说也解释恐龙崛起
sentences: Everybody knows that the dinosaurs became extinct as a result of a large asteroid; something big hit the Earth 65 million years ago and, when the dust had fallen, so had the great reptiles.
众所周知，一颗巨大的小行星使恐龙灭绝。6500万年前，一个庞然大物撞上地球，尘埃落定时，那些巨型爬行动物也已倒下。
There is thus a nice, if ironic, symmetry in the idea that a similar impact brought about the dinosaurs’ rise.
如果恐龙的兴起也是一场类似的撞击造成的，那么这一兴一灭便形成了有趣而带有讽刺意味的对称。
That is the thesis proposed by Paul Olsen of Columbia University.
这就是哥伦比亚大学保罗·奥尔森提出的论点。
paragraphs.gist: 奥尔森提出一个与恐龙灭绝成因相呼应的假说：类似的小行星撞击也可能曾为恐龙的崛起创造条件。

paragraphs.brief: 恐龙在地质瞬间取得优势
sentences: Dinosaurs first appear in the fossil record 230 million years ago, during the Triassic period.
化石记录显示，恐龙最早出现在 2.3 亿年前的三叠纪。
But they were mostly small, and they shared the Earth with lots of other sorts of reptile.
不过，当时的恐龙大多体形很小，与许多其他爬行动物共同生活在地球上。
It was in the subsequent Jurassic period, which began 202 million years ago, that they overran the planet and turned into the monsters realistically depicted in modern books and movies.
直到随后开始于2.02亿年前的侏罗纪，恐龙才遍布地球，长成今天书籍和电影中逼真呈现的庞然大物。
Dr Olsen and his colleagues are not the first to suggest that the dinosaurs inherited the Earth as the result of an asteroid strike.
奥尔森博士及其同事并非最先提出小行星撞击使恐龙统治地球的人。
But they are the first to show that the takeover did, indeed, happen in a geological eye-blink.
但他们最先证明，这场更替在地质时间尺度上确实发生于转瞬之间。
paragraphs.gist: 恐龙在三叠纪已出现却多属小型，到侏罗纪才主宰地球，奥尔森团队首次用证据表明这一更替在地质尺度上极为迅速。

paragraphs.brief: 北美湖岸为何适于研究足印
sentences: Dinosaur skeletons are rare.
恐龙骨架相当罕见。
Dinosaur footprints are, however, surprisingly abundant.
然而，恐龙的足迹却惊人地丰富。
And the size of the prints is as good an indication of the size of the beasts as are the skeletons themselves.
足印的大小和骨架一样，能很好地反映动物的体形。
Dr Olsen and his colleagues therefore concentrated on prints, not bones.
因此，奥尔森博士和同事把注意力放在足印上，而非骨骼上。
The prints in question were made in Eastern North America, a part of the world then full of rift valleys similar to those in East Africa today.
这些足印留在北美东部，那里当时布满裂谷，类似今天的东非。
Like the modern African rift valleys, the Triassic/Jurassic American ones contained lakes, and these lakes grew and shrank at regular intervals because of climatic changes.
和现代非洲裂谷一样，三叠纪至侏罗纪的北美裂谷里也有湖泊，因气候变化而有规律地涨落。
Rocks from this place and period can be dated to within a few thousand years.
这一地区、这一时期的岩石可以测年，误差范围在数千年以内。
As a bonus, squishy lake-edge sediments are just the things for recording the tracks of passing animals.
此外，湖边松软潮湿的沉积物恰好能记录路过动物的足迹。
paragraphs.gist: 与罕见的骨架相比，足印丰富且能反映体型，北美东部裂谷湖岸松软的沉积物又能保存足迹，岩层年代也较易确定。

paragraphs.brief: 以遗迹分类追踪动物群
sentences: By dividing the labour between them, the research team were able to study such tracks at 80 sites and look at 18 so-called ‘ichnotaxa’.
研究团队分工合作，考察了80处地点的足迹，辨认出18种所谓的“遗迹分类单元”。
These are recognisable types of footprint that cannot be matched precisely within the species of animal that left them.
这些足印各具可辨认的形态，却无法精确确定留下它们的动物属于哪个物种。
But they can be matched with a general sort of animal, and thus act as an indicator of the fate of that group, even when there are no bones to tell the story.
不过，足印能对应到某一大类动物，即使没有骨骼，也可以用来追踪这个动物类群的命运。
paragraphs.gist: 团队在八十个地点比较十八种可辨足迹类型，虽难精确判断是哪一物种所留，却能在没有骨骼时追踪某类动物的兴衰。

paragraphs.brief: 地层交界的足迹和异常信号
sentences: Their findings show that five of the ichnotaxa disappear before the end of the Triassic, and four march confidently across the boundary into the Jurassic.
结果显示，五种足迹类型在三叠纪结束前已经消失，另有四种明显跨过地层界线，延续到侏罗纪。
Six, however, vanish at the boundary, or only just splutter across it; and three appear from nowhere, almost as soon as the Jurassic begins.
另有六种在交界处消失，或仅勉强延续过界线；还有三种此前不见踪影，却在侏罗纪开始时几乎立刻出现。
That boundary itself is suggestive.
这条地层界线本身也颇有启示。

The first geological indication of the impact that killed the dinosaurs was an unusually high level of iridium in rocks at the end of the Cretaceous period, when the beasts disappear from the fossil record.
导致恐龙灭绝的撞击最初是由地质证据提示的：白垩纪末、也就是恐龙从化石记录中消失之时的岩石里，铱含量异常之高。
Iridium is normally rare at the Earth’s surface, but it is more abundant in meteorites.
铱在地球表面通常很稀少，在陨石中却较为丰富。
When people began to believe the impact theory, they started looking for other Cretaceous-end anomalies.
撞击假说逐渐被人接受后，研究者开始寻找白垩纪末的其他异常现象。
One that turned up was a surprising abundance of fern spores in rocks just above the boundary layer – a phenomenon known as the ‘fern spike’.
他们发现，界线层正上方的岩石中蕨类孢子异常丰富，这种现象称为“蕨类孢子峰”。
paragraphs.gist: 多种足迹在三叠纪末消失，新类型随即出现；研究者还借白垩纪末异常丰富的铱和蕨类孢子说明如何寻找撞击线索。

paragraphs.brief: 蕨类孢子激增指示灾变
sentences: That matched the theory nicely.
这一发现与撞击假说吻合得很好。
Many modern ferns are opportunists.
许多现代蕨类善于抓住环境变化带来的机会。
They cannot compete against plants with leaves, but if a piece of land is cleared by, say, a volcanic eruption, they are often the first things to set up shop there.
它们争不过其他有叶植物，但如果火山喷发等事件清空一片土地，它们往往最先在那里生长。
An asteroid strike would have scoured much of the Earth of its vegetable cover, and provided a paradise for ferns.
小行星撞击会扫除地球大部分地区的植被，给蕨类留下非常有利的生长环境。
A fern spike in the rocks is thus a good indication that something terrible has happened.
因此，岩石中出现蕨类孢子峰，是曾发生重大灾变的有力迹象。
paragraphs.gist: 蕨类擅长率先占据受扰动的裸地，撞击若清除大片植被便会创造有利条件，岩层中孢子骤增因此可提示重大灾变。

sentences: The surprises are how rapidly the new ichnotaxa appeared and how quickly they increased in size.
出人意料的是，新的足迹类型出现得很快，足印尺寸随之迅速增大。
Dr Olsen and his colleagues suggest that the explanation for this may be a phenomenon called ecological release.
奥尔森博士和他的同事建议，对此的解释可能是一种称为生态释放的现象。
This is seen today when reptiles (which in modern times tend to be small creatures) reach islands where they face no competitors.
今天，当爬行动物(在现代往往是小生物)到达没有竞争对手的岛屿时，就可以看到这一点。
The most spectacular example is on the Indonesian island of Komodo, where local lizards have grown so large that they are often referred to as dragons.
最引人注目的例子是印度尼西亚科莫多岛，那里的当地蜥蜴长得如此大，常常被称为龙。
The dinosaurs, in other words, could flourish only when the competition had been knocked out.
换言之，恐龙是在竞争者被淘汰后才得以兴盛的。
paragraphs.gist: 奥尔森用“生态释放”解释恐龙足迹为何迅速变大，如同科莫多岛巨蜥，竞争者消失后原本受限制的类群便能繁盛。

paragraphs.brief: 古撞击坑为何难以寻获
sentences: That leaves the question of where the impact happened.
因此，剩下的问题是撞击究竟发生在哪里。
No large hole in the Earth’s crust seems to be 202 million years old.
地壳上似乎没有哪一个巨大的撞击坑是距今 2.02 亿年前形成的。
It may, of course, have been overlooked.
当然，它可能被忽略了。
Old craters are eroded and buried, and not always easy to find.
古老的撞击坑会被侵蚀或掩埋，因此并不总是容易辨认。
Alternatively, it may have vanished.
或者，它可能已经消失。
Although continental crust is more or less permanent, the ocean floor is constantly recycled by the tectonic processes that bring about continental drift.
虽然大陆地壳或多或少是永久性的，但洋底不断被导致大陆漂流的构造过程所回收。
There is no ocean floor left that is more than 200 million years old, so a crater that formed in the ocean would have been swallowed up by now.
距今超过两亿年的古老洋底已经不复存在，因此，即使当年的撞击坑位于海洋中，如今也应已随洋底一同消失。
paragraphs.gist: 尚未找到约二亿零二百万年前的大撞击坑，它可能被侵蚀和掩埋，也可能位于后来因板块运动而被回收的古海底。

paragraphs.brief: 重新检验魁北克巨坑的年代
sentences: There is a third possibility, however.
但是，还有第三种可能性。
This is that the crater is known, but has been misdated.
也有可能是，撞击坑早已为人所知，只是年代测错了。
The Manicouagan ‘structure’, a crater in Quebec, is thought to be 214 million years old.
曼尼古根“构造”是魁北克的一处陨石坑，估计形成于 2.14 亿年前。

It is huge – some 100 kilometres across – and seems to be the largest of between three and five craters that formed within a few hours of each other as the lumps of disintegrated comet hit the Earth one by one.
它十分巨大，直径约100公里，似乎是同一次事件形成的三至五个撞击坑中最大的，其中各坑由解体彗星的碎块先后撞上地球，在相隔数小时内形成。
Such an impact would surely have had a perceptible effect on the world, but the rocks from 214 million years ago do not record one.
这样的撞击理应在全球留下明显痕迹，然而距今2.14亿年的岩石并未记录这种影响。
It is possible, therefore, that Manicouagan has been misdated.
因此，曼尼古根撞击坑的年代有可能测错了。
That will be the next thing to check.
这将是接下来要检查的事情。
paragraphs.gist: 另一可能是已知撞击坑定年有误，魁北克马尼夸根巨坑的规模与原定年代的岩层反应不符，使其成为待重新检验的候选地点。

items.en: There is still doubt about the theory that an asteroid strike killed the dinosaurs.
items.zh: 对小行星撞击杀死恐龙的理论仍有疑问
items.why: 原文把小行星致灭绝当作“众所周知”的事实，并未说“仍有怀疑",所以与题干相反。

items.en: Books and the cinema have exaggerated the size of dinosaurs.
items.zh: 书和电影都夸大了恐龙的大小
items.why: 文字说明书籍和电影是“写实地描绘 (realistically)”,并非“硅大"”,与题干矛盾。

items.en: Other scientists have rejected Olsen’s idea of a sudden dinosaur occupation of the Earth.
items.zh: 其他科学家则拒绝奥尔森关于恐龙突然占领地球的想法。
items.why: 文中只说奥尔森并非第一个提出“撞击导致统治” 的人，并说他是第一个证明“发生得很快” 的人。没有信息显示“其他科学家否定/拒绝他 '迅速占据地球' 的观点"。故NG。

items.en: Dinosaur footprints are found more frequently than dinosaur skeletons.
items.zh: 恐龙足迹比恐龙骨骼更常见
items.why: 完整骨架难得，文中接着说恐龙足迹却出乎意料地丰富，印证脚印更常被发现。

items.en: Ichnotaxa offer an exact identification of a dinosaur species.
items.zh: 足迹的遗迹分类能够精确识别恐龙的物种。
items.why: 明说不能精确到“物种”层级，题干“提供精确鉴定" 与原文相反。

items.en: There is evidence that some groups of dinosaurs survived from the Triassic period into the Jurassic period.
items.zh: 有证据显示，某些恐龙类群从三叠纪一直存续到侏罗纪。
items.why: 有“四类足迹跨越边界进入侏罗纪”,证上明有些类群从三旱纪延续到侏罗纪。

items.en: Dr Olsen’s group believe that the sudden increase in the size of dinosaurs may have been due to something known as ________.
items.zh: 奥尔森博士的团队认为，恐龙体形突然变大，可能源于一种叫作________的现象。
items.why: 直接给出术语，解释体型骤增的原因。

items.en: A current example of this can be found on Komodo Island in Indonesia, where some of the lizards are commonly called ________ because of their size.
items.zh: 如今在印度尼西亚的科莫多岛上仍能见到类似现象。当地一些蜥蜴因体形巨大，常被称为________。
items.why: 科莫多岛巨蜥“常被称为 dragons”。

items.en: Apparently, they have grown this big because they do not have any ________.
items.zh: 它们之所以能长到这么大，显然是因为没有________。
items.why: 由于缺乏竞争者而长得更大。

items.en: First, it may have been ________ by scientists, because craters are easily covered up.
items.zh: 第一种可能是，由于陨石坑很容易被掩埋，科学家可能________了它。
items.why: 第一种原因: 可能被忽略。

items.en: Or, it could have ________; for example, if the hole had been in the ocean, it would no longer exist because of the ____ (Q12) that produce continental drift.
items.zh: 第二种可能是，陨石坑已经________。例如，如果坑位于海洋中，造成大陆漂移的________（Q12）就会使它不复存在。
items.why: 第二种原因: 可能已经消失。

items.en: Or, it could have ____ (Q11); for example, if the hole had been in the ocean, it would no longer exist because of the ________ that produce continental drift.
items.zh: 第二种可能是，陨石坑已经________（Q11）。例如，如果坑位于海洋中，造成大陆漂移的________就会使它不复存在。
items.why: 海底被板块构造过程不断回收，故海洋中的陨石坑会不复存在。

items.en: Thirdly, the hole could still exist but have been ________.
items.zh: 第三种可能是，这个坑仍然存在，只是它的年代被________了。
items.why: 第三种原因: 坑存在但被误定年代。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填三个词。

pairs: 两处都引出人们给科莫多岛蜥蜴起的俗称。
两处都涉及能否准确对应到物种。原文用 cannot 否定了题干的判断。
第 7 段 · 第 5 句
第 1 段 · 第 1 句
points: 文字说明书籍和电影是“写实地描绘 (realistically)”,并非“硅大"”,与题干矛盾。
第三种原因: 坑存在但被误定年代。
clauses: … ; something big hit the Earth 65 million years ago and, when the dust had fallen, so had the great reptiles.
“Everybody knows that the dinosaurs became extinct as a result of a large asteroid”补足 hit 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 hit 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
These are recognisable types of footprint ….
“that cannot be matched precisely within the species of animal that left them”修饰前面的 types。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 types，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: The dinosaurs may have risen to power in as little as 10,000 years.
恐龙或许只用了一万年，就成为地球上的优势动物。
vocabulary: 生态释放（竞争等约束消失）
